why: Russell's chapter turns on one example, the sunrise, and one counterexample, the chicken.

cards.claim: We all expect the sun to rise tomorrow; the question is whether that belief is reasonable.
src: We are all convinced that the sun will rise to-morrow. Why?

examples.label: The chicken
src: the farmer who has fed the chicken every day finally wrings its neck

cards.claim: Past regularities are only a cause of expectation, not yet a reason for it.
src: Experience has shown us that, hitherto, the frequent repetition of some uniform succession or coexistence has been a _cause_ of our expecting the same succession

lenses.title: Share of the chapter about the sun

steps.label: Laplace's rule of succession
src: the sun has risen a million times, so it will rise again

nodes.text: The principle of induction cannot be proved by experience.

people.name: David Hume
src: as Hume showed, the problem of induction cannot be solved
